text:
Justin Barron is on his fourth NHL team at 25, and the Blues might be the one that gets him. He has 14 points in 20 games, a pace four times last season's, and STLtoday wrote this week that he's among the most productive defensemen in the league.

The question is how much holds. Our numbers are cautious: he's scoring on 14.3% of his shots, more than double a typical defenseman, and his eight points in the last ten came on 4.1 expected. The talent range has his true scoring rate well below where he's running.

The real gains are the ice time, up to 16:33 a night from 14:15, and a power-play look the team has started to give him. St. Louis has won six of his last ten, and Barron was part of the rush through the 8-6 and 9-6 wins.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a mixed picture: he stopped 16% of the zone entries aimed at him last season, better than typical, but kept possession on only 30% of his exits. What to watch: whether the minutes keep growing once the shooting cools.
